articles.title: September 2026 Player of the Month announced
articles.meta: Sat 10th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The Winners of the Player of the Month Awards for September 2026 have been announced by the NWCFL.

PREMIER DIVISION

The North West Counties League Premier Division Player of the Month Award for September 2026 has gone to Oliver Hodgson of Longridge Town.

Oliver came through at Burnley and made his debut in the NWCFL as a 16-year old at Nelson. After two seasons there he moved to Bacup Borough after two seasons to continue his development under Brent Peters. He was named Player of the Month in the First Division North in December 2025. This past summer he moved to Bury as part of their newly established Emerging Talent Group, and joined Longridge in August on a season long loan.

September was a phenomenal month for Oliver who played in all six games that his side played in the month. He scored in every single game, nothing up ten goals in total. He scored once in the games at Irlam and Charnock Richard as well as one in their home game with Glossop North End. He found the net twice in their game at Atherton LR, and also scored twice at AFC Liverpool to give his side a 2-1 win.

His best in the month though was scoring a hat-trick in his sides win at home to Abbey Hey, a game that also saw him named as Man of the Match by Abbey Hey due to his performance.

Congratulations Oliver!

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

The First Division North Player of the Month for September 2026 goes to Barney Wiggin of Colne.

Barney came through the ranks at FC Halifax Town before switching to Colne at the start of last season which is his first senior club. He soon established himself as a key member of the team and has really kicked on this season. This is the first time Barney has won this award.

September saw Barney play in all eight games that Colne played. He found the net in six of those games, scoring nine goals in total. He hit the only goal in the opening game against Bacup before scoring the second in a 2-0 win at Squires Gate. He also won Man of the Match in that game. The highlight of the month came as Colne thrashed Darwen 6-0, Barney getting a hat-trick as well as winning Man of the Match.

He scored in the 2-0 win at Tow Law Town in the FA Vase and then the equaliser at home to Holker Old Boys in a 1-1 draw. Barney picked up his third Man of the Match in that game also. He also found the net twice against Bamber Bridge in Colne's 4-3 loss in the Lancashire Trophy.

Congratulations to Barney on a fine month.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

The First Division South Player of the Month for September 2026 goes to forward Daniel Clarkson of Stafford Town.

Daniel came through the ranks at Chasetown and joined Stafford at the start of this season to help continue his development. He is certainly doing that if September is anything to go by!

His best position is deep lying midfielder, constantly breaking down opposition attacks and setting Stafford on their way forward. He did this excellently in the first two games of the month which enabled his team to record home victories over Allscott Heath and Alsager Town. Daniel was named as the opposition Man of the Match in both of these games, as well as grabbing an assist in each of them.

Daniel was also instrumental in the 3-3 draw at Cheadle Heath Nomads as Stafford twice came from behind to grab a point, claiming another assist for Staffords third goal of the afternoon.

Congratulations Daniel!

articles.title: Emirates FA Cup Final Qualifying Round Draw
articles.meta: Mon 5th October 2026 | FA Competition News | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The draw has taken place for the Final Qualifying Round of the Emirates FA Cup.

Of the 19 Premier Division clubs that entered the Emirates FA Cup this season, we are down to just one with Trafford still in the competition. They face a replay at Atherton Collieries tomorrow evening following their 2-2 draw on Saturday, with a victory ensuring that they will reach this round for the first time in their history.

Should they win at Colls, then they will be just 90 minutes away from a place in the First Round Proper. And standing in their way would be an away trip to AFC Fylde.

AFC Fylde are in the National League this season, and they have started the season well with a current league placing of seventh. They have won six of the twelve league games that they have played but unusually they have won just one of them at home with two draws and two losses in their other games. Fylde have not played in the FA Cup this season as National League sides only enter at this round.

The two sides have met just three times in the past. The first two were in 2010/11 in the Northern Premier League when Flyde were on their climb up the football pyramid. Both sides won their home games, with Flyde winning 2-1 and Trafford winning 2-0. The only other meeting came in the Preliminary Round of the FA Trophy in 2011/12, with Fylde winning 4-1 away at Trafford.

The ties is set to be played on the weekend of Saturday, 17 October.

The draw including our sides can be found below:

FOURTH QUALIFYING ROUND

SATURDAY 17 OCTOBER 2026

WINNERS RECEIVE £9,375

LOSERS RECEIVE £3,125

16. AFC Fylde v Atherton Collieries or Trafford

articles.title: Trafford - PST Sport Premier Division Club of the Month
articles.meta: Tue 6th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Trafford have been presented with their PST Sport Club of the Month award for August 2026. League Director Martin Fallon made his way to last midweek's league game with Burscough where he is pictured presenting the framed certificate to Trafford Secretary Paul Delaney.

After relegation from the Northern Premier League last season, Trafford have started the season well in their return to the NWCFL. They have played five league games, winning four of them and losing one, as well as progressing in the Emirates FA Cup with two wins, one of which was against a side from the league above.

They started the season in convincing style with a 3-0 home win against Longridge Town. Ryan Brooke scored their first goal of the season midway through the first half with Kyle Worsley and Finley Stanyer adding to the score in the second half. Their first away game was at last seasons runners-up Ramsbottom United, this the only blip on an otherwise perfect month as they lost 3-0.

They bounced back with progress in the Emirates FA Cup with a trip to Northern Counties East side Worsbrough Bridge Athletic, with Scott Sephton and Harry Norris goals securing a 2-0 win. A week later was another Northern Counties East side as they travelled to Armthorpe Welfare in the FA Vase, Bile Ahmed putting them ahead on the stroke of half time. Luke Sephton added a second on the hour with Kyle Worsley scoring the third, before Ahmed secured a 4-0 win in stoppage time with his second goal of the game.

A return to league action came next in what was their fourth successive away game, a trip to Abbey Hey. First half goals from Luke Sephton and Dillon Edmundson put them in control, with Sephton getting his second of the game in stoppage time for a 3-0 win.

The highlight of the month for Trafford came next as they travelled to Runcorn Linnets in the Emirates FA Cup. It was especially memorable for Ryan Brooke, who is the all time leading goalscorer at the Northern Premier League side, and he put Trafford ahead against his former club after just seven minutes. Jensen Bowering increased the lead after 19 minutes with David Worrall making it three at the start of the second half. Linnets hit back and then added a second in stoppage time, but Trafford held on for a famous win.

The final game of the month came with a home game against FC Isle of Man, their first at home since the opening day. Ryan Brooke scored the only goal of the game in a 1-0 win to ensure a solid month for Trafford.

Those results gave them 23 points towards the Club of the Month calculation from their 7 games for a 3.29 average.

The closest challengers were Nelson who have started the season well after promotion last season. Fellow promoted side Droylsden were also up there as were Prestwich Heys.

Total Games played in the Month: 7Total Points won in the Month: 23Average: 3.25

First Division North - Maghull

Club of the Month in the First Division North is Maghull, who have once again started the season in blistering fashion.

Maghull sit proudly at the top of the league at the end of August. After losing their first game of the season, they romped to victory in their next eight games, scoring a whopping 26 goals in the month and conceded just eight.

They started the season with a trip to Darwen with Nathan Moffitt putting them ahead on 7 minutes. However the home side turned it around to win 2-1 with two late goals, the winner coming just two minutes from time.

They bounced back with a 1-0 home win against AFC Blackpool, Jamie Clark's penalty on 69 minutes the difference, before beating Holker Old Boys 4-1 at home. Holker took an early lead with Wil Hoey levelling before the break. Connor Rankin put Maghull ahead just before the hour, with two late goals from Sam Smith giving them the win.

Next came an impressive 3-0 midweek win at Ashton Town, Sam Smith scoring once in each half with a penalty from Jamie Clark in stoppage time being the icing on the cake. A trip to Uppermill was next and they fell behind in the first half. However Ayden Garrigan levelled after an hour with Connor Rankin scoring the winner for Maghull in a 2-1 win in the last minute of the game.

Maghull's next game was at home to Ashton Athletic with Nathan Moffitt putting them ahead midway through the half. However just a minute later Ashton levelled. Sam Smith's fifth goal of the season put them back ahead before half time, with Nathan Peet and Jacob Till securing a 4-1 win in the second half. A third clean sheet of the month came at Garstang next in a 3-0 win. Connor Rankin scored just after half an hour, with another Jamie Clark penalty making it 2-0 six minutes into the second half. Nathan Peet scored the final goal

Perhaps the performance of the month came in the next game at home to Maine Road, a 5-1 victory being their biggest of the month. They went ahead through Connor Rankin on 16 minutes with their opponents levelling shortly after. It stayed that was until just after the hour when a quickfire double from Nathan Moffitt put them in control before Rankin added his second of the game with 20 minutes to go. A Harry Long goal in the last minute outlined their superiority.

The final game came at home to AFC Knowsley on Bank Holiday Monday, with a superb crowd of 455 watching what was a local derby. Knowsley took an early lead before a double from Nathan Peet turned things around, although scores were level at the break when Knowsley equalised just before the break. Maghull secured what was their eighth successive win with Connor Rankin making it 3-2 on the hour.

That gave them 27 points from their 9 games for a 3.00 average.

Cammell Laird 1907 had a good month after their switch to the North with five wins and two draws in their eight games. Woolton had four wins and three draws, with Darwen also having four wins in the month.

Total Games played in the Month: 9Total Points won in the Month: 27Average: 3.00

First Division South - AFC Bridgnorth

The winner of the Club of the Month in the First Division South are AFC Bridgnorth, their first month in the NWCFL being impressive after being laterally moved from the Midland League.

They spoke pre-season that the move to our league could benefit them with more local games than last season, and they have started the season with five wins and two draws from their seven games. They have also done it in style with 20 goals scored, scoring three or more goals in five of their seven games in the month.

Their first NWCFL game came at home to Foley Meir, with Sam Preece scoring in first half stoppage time to open their account. Foley levelled in the opening stages of the second half, but a late double from Suar Dedja - both goals coming in the final six minutes - gave them their first three points.

It was a win that obviously gave them confidence, as a midweek trip to Bilston Town saw them return with a 4-0 win. Kobi Love put them ahead on 20 minutes before another quick Suar Dedja double made it three, this time his goals coming in the last five minutes of the first half. A strong performance was highlighted when Craig Tuckley added a fourth midway through the second half.

The third game was Bilston Town again, this time at home in the Edward Case Cup. It looked like a repeat was on the cards with Mitchell Evans and Craig Tuckley making it 2-0 with less than an hour played, however Bilston hit back this time to secure a 2-2 draw. That meant penalties with AFC Bridgnorth winning 4-1 from the spot. Their first league points were dropped in the next game which was a 1-1 draw at Wednesfield Community. The home side went ahead with just 18 minutes to go, but Bridgnorth showed their grittiness with a leveller four minutes later.

They returned to winning ways with a 4-1 win at home to Crewe, but it was not all plain sailing, especially when Crewe went ahead after two minutes. Michael Williams levelled after 15 minutes, and it remained that way until Suar Dedja put them ahead on 64 minutes. It took a late double from Nehemia Zazi to secure the win, both his goals coming in the last ten minutes.

A trip to Alsager Town was next, with the home side taking the lead before Suar Dedja's penalty on the half hour making it one each. Bridgnorth went in at the break ahead with Sam Preece scoring just before the whistle, and Preece then made it 3-1 at the start of the second half. Another from Alsager just after the hour made it interesting, but they could not find an equalier, Bridgnorth winning 3-2.

The seventh final game of the month saw them host New Mills, another game where they won 3-2 but this time having to twice come from behind. The Millers scored early before Suar Dedja equalised on 17 minutes. Just before half time New Mills went ahead only for Mitchell Evans to level just before the hour. With a draw looking likely, David Anani hit the winner three minutes from time.

That gave them 20 points from their 7 games for a 2.86 average.

Closest to them was Eccleshall with six wins from eight games, with Wolverhampton Casuals winning five of their seven games. Brereton Social also started well with three wins before tailing off as the month progressed.

Total Games played in the Month: 7Total Points won in the Month: 20Average: 2.86

Congratulations to all of the winners.

articles.title: Connor Beard - Premier Division Goalkeeper of the Month
articles.meta: Tue 6th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Connor Beard has been presented with his paxsport Goalkeeper of the Month award for August 2026. The Trafford goalkeeper was presented with his award prior to Saturday's FA Cup tie with Atherton Collieries by League Chairman Chris Stirrup, with Club Secretary Paul Delaney looking on.

This is the first time that Connor has won this award and also the first win for Trafford - hardly surpringly though given that they have not been in our league since the 2007/08 season! Connor's performances for Trafford has helped them to win the Club of the Month, with Connor keeping five clean sheets in seven games played.

Connor made the switch to the Trafford at the start of this season after previous being at Abbey Hey, making 42 appearances last season as Abbey firmly established themselves as a Premier Division side. Previous to that he was at Atherton LR, whilst he has also played in the league for Sandbach United.

The first game in August saw Trafford host Longridge Town. It was a comfortable afternoon for Connor who kept a clean sheet in a 3-0 win. The following midweek game was less comfortable, with Rambottom United winning 3-0, all three goals coming in the first half. Connor could do little with any, one being a deflected own goal and another a long range, dipping effort.

Another clean sheet came in Connor's third game, marshalling his defence well in a 2-0 win in the FA Cup at Worsbrough Bridge Athletic. When he was beaten, the ball rebounded off the crossbar. Two clean sheets then became three as Trafford progressed in the FA Vase with a 4-0 win at Armthorpe Welfare.

Trafford returned to league action with a 3-0 win at Abbey Hey, that being three successive clean sheets for Connor. Abbey offered strong resistance in this game, but again Connor's organisation of his defence was imperitive.

A 3-2 win at Runcorn Linnets was next in the Emirates FA Cup, Connor unable to prevent either of Linnets' goals. The final game brought a fourth clean sheet of the month, Trafford taking an early lead and being thankful for Connor's form as he kept out efforts from Dean Pinnington and Tomas Brown.

Six games in the month, four clean sheets and just seven goals conceded.

Congratulations to Connor on his Award!

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 10
articles.meta: Thu 8th October 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Another week, another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. The last FA Cup domino falls

It has been a valiant effort, but unfortunately, Trafford were beaten on Tuesday in their Third Qualifying Round replay away from home against higher-division Atherton Collieries. With that, there are no NWCFL teams left in English football’s oldest competition for the 2026/27 campaign.

Tom Baker’s team got further than any other side from the NWCFL, knocking off Worsbrough Bridge Athletic, Runcorn Linnets, Bamber Bridge and Heaton Stannington before falling at the feat of their NPL Division One West opponents in midweek – don’t cry because it’s over, and all that.

2. The Edward Case Cup proper returns

Since the weekend, there have been several matches in the Edward Case Cup first round proper, nearly two months removed from the preliminary fixtures held in early August. There have already been some headline-grabbing results in the early stages of this year’s competition, including…

Flixton proving their mettle in an all-First Division North clash on home soil against Darwen, which they won 5-3; First Division South promotion chasers Thornton Cleveleys laying down the gauntlet in a 5-1 away drubbing of newly promoted Uppermill; and Barnton surprising the life out of First Division South play-off hopefuls Eccleshall with a 6-0 write-off.

3. Linnets with the longest loss-less streak

It is a pretty great time to be a regular watcher of Burscough right now. Following their 3-2 victory over Glossop North End on Saturday, they are unbeaten in their last six games in all competitions, and have only dropped points once during that stretch of games – and even then, it was a game that took place halfway across the Irish Sea, at the Bowl, home of play-off candidates FC Isle of Man.

Their weekend victory takes them to the top of the form table in the Premier Division and also sees them reclaim second place outright in the table from Droylsden, who were beaten in Saturday’s battle of the top two by Nelson. The Linnets are not letting go in the early stages of this title race.

4. Mechanics struggling with homesickness

Only one side is keeping AFC Blackpool from propping up the First Division North, and that is winless Uppermill, on goal difference alone. The seaside outfit have had a tough go of things in the league from their opening 12 games, and nowhere is this better exemplified than in their away record in 2026/27.

In two-thirds of their league games so far, they’ve been the visiting side, and they are yet to earn a point on the road as we move into October. Their match this past weekend was another away from the Mechanics Ground, and another that saw them return home empty-handed, having been beaten 4-0 by Ashton Town. With any luck this is a run that will end this coming Saturday, as they face their fellow members of the bottom-two club on away soil.

5. Second season success for Wolves Casuals?

Last season was very much a transitional one for Wolverhampton Casuals. Their lateral move to the NWCFL took some time to adjust to, but the team from Brinsford Stadium found their feet as the season got older, and eventually finished a relatively comfortable, certainly stable, 14th in the league, and nine points ahead of the drop zone.

This season, going by their opening 10 games, they have much higher aspirations. Between Saturday and Monday, they won twice in 48 hours, knocking off Wednesfield Community in the league to stabilise themselves in the silver medal spot in the table, and following that with progression in the Edward Case Cup by seeing off Cheadle Heath Nomads. This could be a season to remember for Wolves Casuals.

articles.title: Nicky Parker - First Division South Player of the Month
articles.meta: Thu 8th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Nicky Parker of Eccleshall was presented with his August 2026 First Division South Player of the Month award ahead of his teams last home game with AFC Bridgnorth. Nicky is pictured receiving his award from League Ambassador Andrew Reid.

This is the second successive award for Nicky, who won this award for Eccleshall in April last season. Nicky is a prolific goalscorer who scored 33 goals in 59 games for Market Drayton Town before switching to Eccleshall at the start of last season. He hit 20 goals last season, helping Eccleshall finish as Runners Up in the league before they heartbreakingly lost in the Play-Off Final on penalties. He has previously played for former NWCFL side Whitchurch Alport in the Midland League, as well as Prees United in the Shropshire County League.

The first game in saw Eccleshall win 3-1 at home to newcomers Widnes Town. Nicky caused problems for the visiting defence throughout and scored the second goal of the game to put his side 2-0 up and give them some breathing space. His performance led to him winning Man of the Match in this game.

Eccleshall's first clean sheet of the season came next in midweek with a 4-0 win at Allscott Heath. Nicky was again instrumental in the victory as he caused problems all night for Allscott. He opened the scoring just after the half hour and added a second before the break. He then set up teammate Levi Hunter at the start of the second half to make it three, allowing Eccleshall to take their foot off the gas a little. Once again he won Man of the Match.

Barnton defeated Eccleshall in Nicky's next game 2-1, before they bounced back with a 2-1 win of their own at Wolverhampton Casuals. No goals for Nicky in these two games, but he did set up Morgan Russell for the winner in the Wolves game just after half time, his overall performance again seeing him win Man of the Match.

Another 4-0 win followed with victory over Allscott Heath again, this time in the FA Vase. Nicky was on target for the second goal in this game as his side progressed to the next round. Nicky's final game of the month came with a 3-2 home loss to Wednesfield Community. After going three goals down, Eccleshall rallied with Nicky's fifth goal of the season getting them back into it, but they couldn't force a draw.

Six games for Nicky in the month, five of which was in the league where he won Man of the Match four times. He also scored five goals in the month.

Congratulations Nicky!

articles.title: Adam Whitehouse - First Division South Goalkeeper of the Month
articles.meta: Thu 8th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Adam Whirehouse has been presented with his paxsport Goalkeeper of the Month award for August 2026. The Eccleshall goalkeeper was presented with his award prior to Saturday's game with AFC Bridgnorth by League Ambassador Andrew Reid.

Adam played more than 200 times for the Stafford Rangers after first joining the club in 2014, and was part of the Stafford side that won the 2015/16 Northern Premier League First Division South. After leaving Stafford, he played for Boldmere St. Michaels and Rushall Olympic before moving to Hanley Town and then Newcastle Town. He joined Eccleshall last October from Newcastle, quickly establishing himself as the clubs' number one.

Eccleshall started the season with a 3-1 home win against Widnes Town, Adam unable to do anything to stop Josh Quarless' consolation with ten minutes remaining. The midweek game at Allscott Heath saw him keep a clean sheet in a 4-0 win.

Barnton then won 2-1 at Eccleshall, Adam again with no chance for either goal, and it could have been more but for a superb stop from a Joe Keyworth effort.

Eccleshall returned to winning ways with a 4-0 win over Allscott Heath in the FA Vase, a second clean sheet of the season. Wednesfield Community then stunned Eccleshall with a 3-2 win, Eccleshall going three behind there as they switched off for the first hour of that game.

The final two games of the month were both similar. Both were won 1-0 on the road at Foley Meir and Cheadle Heath Nomads, with Adam making it four clean sheets in the month. He marshalled his defence well in both games, being alert when required to keep the home sides at bay.

In total seven games played with four clean sheets and just six goals conceded.

Congratulations Adam!

articles.title: Barnton Celebrate 80 Years
articles.meta: Thu 8th October 2026 | Barnton | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Barnton AFC is celebrating a very special milestone this weekend, 80 years of football in the village. They are inviting the whole Barnton community to join them at their home game with Dawley Town for what promises to be a truly memorable day.

The club are especially inviting all former players, managers and everyone who has played a part in the history of Barnton football to come along, reunite with old friends and help them celebrate eight decades of memories.

Football has always been about much more than what happens on the pitch. For generations, Barnton has brought families, friends and the wider community together, giving people of all ages the opportunity to play, support, volunteer and simply enjoy the beautiful game.

There have been far too many fantastic memories, characters and stories over the past 80 years to mention them all, but now it’s time to celebrate their history and, most importantly, make sure football in Barnton continues for another 80 years and beyond.

To mark the occasion, Barnton AFC will wear a special red third kit, inspired by the club’s original colours from 1946.

Barnton Juniors will be the mascots, representing the next generation and the future of the club.

There will be plenty happening throughout the day, with the bar open from 1pm, the kitchen serving food, plus a Cheshire Dough pizza van and MerryFall Cakes on site.

Kick off is at 3.00pm.

Whether you wore the famous black and white, pulled on a Barnton shirt many years ago, stood on the sidelines as a manager, coach, volunteer or supporter, or are part of the Barnton football family today, the club want you there.&

Come along, show your support and help the club celebrate their 80th birthday on a day to remember.

80 YEARS. ONE CLUB. ONE COMMUNITY.

articles.title: Daniel Jennings - First Division North Goalkeeper of the Month
articles.meta: Fri 9th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Daniel Jennings has been presented with his paxsport Goalkeeper of the Month award for August 2026. The Woolton goalkeeper was presented with his award prior to Saturday's game with Uppermill by League Director Martin Fallon.

Daniel is the first Woolton player to win this award, and it is the first time that Daniel has won this award. He is in his second season in the NWCFL and has represented Woolton since their promotion to the league at the start of last season. He has been at the club for a number of years having come through at MSB Woolton Reserves in the Liverpool Premier League.

The first game for Daniel in the month came at Colne, conceding just once as Woolton started the season with a 3-1 win. Next up was a home game against Ashton Town with Woolton making it a perfect start with a 3-2 win.

A trip to Darwen was next, Daniel saving early on from Daniel Basterfield. With the scores at 1-1, Daniel made key saves from Basterfield again, Ryan Cattermole and Nathan Bond to secure his side a point. The first clean sheet of the month for Daniel came next in a goalless draw with Ashton Athletic. Daniel organised his defensive well, and when he was beaten, saw Marcus Cusani's shot come back off the crossbar.

Another clean sheet came in a 1-0 FA Vase win against AFC Liverpool. Daniel set the groundwork with good saves from Aaron Cummins and Kyle Robinson-Murray, laying the foundations for a 1-0 win.

Woolton were then involved in two 2-1 scorelines, with a defeat at home to Ashville and a win at Daisy Hill. Daniel could do little to stop any of the three goals, but made a key save late on against Daisy Hill from Gerry McCullion, fortunately seeing the rebound disallowed for offside.

The final game was a 3-3 thriller with Squires Gate, Woolton coming from 2-0 and 3-1 down. Daniel made several key stops early in the game to prevent Gate running away with it, giving his side the opportunity to come back to force a point.

In total Daniel played eight games and kept two clean sheets, with just ten goals conceded.

Congratulations to Daniel for his performances in the month!

articles.title: Toby Green - Premier Division Player of the Month
articles.meta: Fri 9th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Toby Green of Prestwiich Heys was presented with his August 2026 Premier Division Player of the Month award ahead of his teams last home game. Toby is pictured receiving his award from League Committee Member Sid Blain.

This is the second time that he has won this award after picking it up in February 2025 when playing for Stockport Town. It is the first win for Prestwich since Jamie Hill won it in January 2020.

Toby came through the ranks at Stockport County where he progressed to their National League U19 Alliance team before moving to Stockport Town ahead of the 2021/22 season. After two seasons he switched to Droylsden and then Abbey Hey before returning to Stockport Town in for the 2024/25 season. He remained there until they dropped out of the league last season with Prestwich moving quickly to get his signature at the start of this season.

The opening day of the season was one of disappointment for Heys as they went down 4-1 at Burscough. Toby did his bit on the day, winning Man of the Match for his team including an assist for Louis Holt's goal. The frustration continued with a 1-1 draw against Barnoldswick Town, Toby again getting an assist for Heys' goal when his corner was was met by captain James Badrock to score. He also went close to a winner with three minutes remaining, his free kick rebounding off the post.

The FA Cup was next, Toby helping his side to their first clean sheet of the season with a 2-0 win. And next up was Heys' first league win of the season as they beat Glossop North End 2-0, Toby winning his second Man of the Match award with a hand in both goals. The first saw him set up right back Reece Higgins, whose strike gave him his first senior goal. The second saw him convert a penalty to put his side two goals ahead.

Next was another FA Cup game at Runcorn Town. Toby got his name on the scoresheet here for the second game running when he fired in a shot from twelve yards to make it 2-0, Heys going on to win 3-1. The final game was a 1-1 draw with Charnock Richard, with Toby again winning Man of the Match for his performance. After Heys' early goal, Toby went close to a second when he struck the post, and set up several opportunities for teammates throughout the game.

He played six games in total, winning Man of the Match in three of the four league games he played and scoring twice.

Congratulations Toby!

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

The First Division North Player of the Month for August 2026 goes to Adam Smith of Cammell Laird 1907, the first time Adam has won this award. We have to go back to September 2019 for the last Lairds winner, that being Kyle Sambor.

Adam came through at West Cheshire League side Mersey Royal before moving to Vauxhall Motors in 2022. He helped them to promotion from the NWCFL and consolidate their position in the Northern Premier League before switching to Buckley Town. Whilst at Buckley he was named in the JD Cymru Leagues North Team of the Season for the 2024/25 campaign. He moved back to the NWCFL with Cammell Laird 1907 last season where he is now an integral part of the team.

In the opening game of the month away at Thornton Cleveleys, Adam caused the home defence problems all afternoon, leading to winning Man of the Match in the game. He opened the scoring after being put clear and slotting past the keeper, then grabbed his second of the game when he chased a long ball over the top and again slotted home. Lairds were unable to hold on though with Thornton hitting back to win 3-2.

A trip to Flixton was next with the home side 2-0 ahead before Lairds made a comeback. Adam hit the equalising goal when he pounced on a mistake at the back just after half time and slotted home, before hitting the winner with four minutes remaining. This was a cross from the right that Adam brought down before finding the top corner.

Adam helped his side to a 2-0 win at home to Squires Gate next, before collecting his second Man of the Match award of the season in a 1-1 draw at AFC Blackpool. Two became three as he won another Man of the Match in his next game, a 3-0 win at home to AFC Knowsley. There were no goals or assists for Adam in these games, but his tireless running caused problems throughout which his team capitalised on.

The next game in the month saw Lairds win 3-2 at home to Fulwood Amateurs. Adam again impressed, winning his third successive Man of the Match and fourth in six league games. He levelled the scores at 1-1 on the stroke of half time with a superb header, and continued to be a nuisance to the visiting defence all afternoon. The last game of the month saw Lairds win 2-1 at Ashton Athletic.

In total, six games for Adam, all of which were in the league, with four Man of the Match wins and five goals scored.

Congratulations to Adam on a fine month.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

The First Division South Player of the Month for August 2026 goes to forward Nicky Parker of Eccleshall.

This is the second successive award for Nicky, who won this award for Eccleshall in April last season. Nicky is a prolific goalscorer who scored 33 goals in 59 games for Market Drayton Town before switching to Eccleshall at the start of last season. He hit 20 goals last season, helping Eccleshall finish as Runners Up in the league before they heartbreakingly lost in the Play-Off Final on penalties. He has previously played for former NWCFL side Whitchurch Alport in the Midland League, as well as Prees United in the Shropshire County League.

The first game in saw Eccleshall win 3-1 at home to newcomers Widnes Town. Nicky caused problems for the visiting defence throughout and scored the second goal of the game to put his side 2-0 up and give them some breathing space. His performance led to him winning Man of the Match in this game.

Eccleshall's first clean sheet of the season came next in midweek with a 4-0 win at Allscott Heath. Nicky was again instrumental in the victory as he caused problems all night for Allscott. He opened the scoring just after the half hour and added a second before the break. He then set up teammate Levi Hunter at the start of the second half to make it three, allowing Eccleshall to take their foot off the gas a little. Once again he won Man of the Match.

Barnton defeated Eccleshall in Nicky's next game 2-1, before they bounced back with a 2-1 win of their own at Wolverhampton Casuals. No goals for Nicky in these two games, but he did set up Morgan Russell for the winner in the Wolves game just after half time, his overall performance again seeing him win Man of the Match.

Another 4-0 win followed with victory over Allscott Heath again, this time in the FA Vase. Nicky was on target for the second goal in this game as his side progressed to the next round. Nicky's final game of the month came with a 3-2 home loss to Wednesfield Community. After going three goals down, Eccleshall rallied with Nicky's fifth goal of the season getting them back into it, but they couldn't force a draw.

Six games for Nicky in the month, five of which was in the league where he won Man of the Match four times. He also scored five goals in the month.

Congratulations Nicky!

articles.title: September 2026 PST Sport Club of the Month
articles.meta: Sat 10th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
We are delighted to confirm our PST Sport Club of the Month winners for September 2026.

PST Sport are a recognised leader in artificial grass pitch construction, delivering complete turnkey solutions for both new build and resurfacing projects. From groundworks and drainage to subbase construction, surfacing, fencing, floodlighting and long-term maintenance, they offer a full-service approach that ensures clubs receive world-class playing surfaces tailored to their needs.

The league have a formula to work out our Club of the Month based on whether games were home and away and the quality of the opposition. Last months winners were are as follows:

Premier Division - Irlam

Winning the Premier Division award for September 2026 is Irlam.

After winning their final game of August, Irlam went on a great run in September with five wins coming from their five matches. Four of these victories came in the Premier Division whilst they also progressed through to the next round of the Macron Cup. They scored 12 goals and conceded just three, whilst they also registered three clean sheets.

The first game in September for Irlam was at home to Longridge Town. They took an early lead through Luke Mann however by half time Longridge had gained the lead with goals from Josh Ashe and Oliver Hodgson. Irlam equalised 20 minutes into the second half through Jacob Holt, with Daniel Dolling putting them ahead ten minutes later. Dolling then hit another with five minutes remaining to give Irlam a 4-2 win.

Next was a home game against last seasons runners-up Ramsbottom United. After a goalless first half, Jack Mitchell put them ahead ten minutes into the second half before Millen Brown added a second in the last minute to record a 2-0 win.

The third game was a trip to Abbey Hey with Irlam taking the lead just before the half hour through Daragh Mulcahy. They added a second goal three minutes into the second half through Abubakar Muhamme, with Omogbolahan Solarin pulling one back midway through the half with 2-1 the final score.

The final league game of the month was a trip to Glossop North End with Irlam running out 3-0 winners. Daniel Dolling opened the scoring on 11 minutes with Ross Davidson doubling the lead on the stroke of halftime. Dolling scored his second of the game five minutes from time to record a convincing win.

The last game of the month was also against Glossop in the Macron Cup. This time it was at Irlam and was much closer with Jack Mitchell scoring the only goal of the game with 15 minutes remaining.

Burscough also had a strong month as did Nelson and Droylsden, but none could match Irlams perfect record.

Total Games played in the Month: 5Total Points won in the Month: 17Average: 3.40

First Division North - Flixton

Club of the Month in the First Division North is Flixton, who like Irlam had a perfect month of five wins from five games.

Their first month back in the NWCFL saw mixed results as they got to terms with the league, but September saw 16 goals scored in the five games with just three conceded. They also kept two clean sheets.

The first game in September was at home to Steeton with Nathan storton giving the visitors the lead just before the half hour. Flixton will level by a half-time though through a Cian Donohue goal with Donohue putting Flixton ahead in the first minute of the second half. Three minutes later Aaron Dwyer added a third with 3-1 the final score.

The next game also finished 3-1 away at Ashton Athletic however it was not a foregone conclusion for much of the match. Ashley Cata put Flixton ahead on 18 minutes with Ashton levelling 17 minutes from time through Josh Brierley. It wasn't until the 88th minute that Flixton regain the lead through Aaron Dwyer with Benni Smalls-Braithwaite adding another in stoppage time.

Next was Woolton at home with Uche Chinohso Eze giving Flixton the lead on 13 minutes. Three minutes later it was two through Lewis-Simon Byrne, with Byrne adding another just before half time. He then completed his hat-trick on 66 minutes to give his side a 4-0 victory.

Lewis-Simon Byrne hit several hat-tricks last season as he scored 63 goals for Chadderton, and he made it successive hat tricks in the next game as Flixton won 3-1 at Garstang. Byrne's three goals all came in the second half with Luke Draysey scoring a consolation for the home side in stoppage time.

The final game saw Uppermill visit Valley Road with an in form Flixton winning 4-0. Benni Smalls-Braithwaite put them ahead after just six minutes with Kieron Molloy adding second on 27 minutes. Smalls-Braithwaite grabbed his second of the game with eight minutes remaining before completing his hat-trick from the penalty spot in stoppage time.

Thornton Cleveleys also had a good month with five just one loss in their seven games, with Maghull, Colne and Woolton also doing well.

Total Games played in the Month: 5Total Points won in the Month: 18Average: 3.60

First Division South - Bilston Town

The winner of the Club of the Month in the First Division South are Bilston Town. Newcomers to the league this season, they have had an impressive start and sit in the play-off positions at present with games in hand on those above them.

They played four games in the month and were unbeaten, with three of those being victories in which they kept a clean sheet and the other a thrilling draw. They scored 15 goals and conceded just three.

The first game came away at Wolverhampton Casuals where they trailed to a Kieran Cook goal after 17 minutes. Callum Bright levelled just after the half hour only for Cook to restore Wolves lead before half time. Cook then made it 3-1 ten minutes into the second half with Harry Dixon pulling one back on 66 minutes. Bilston levelled with seven minutes remaining through Sam Cudjoe Yankson with the game ending 3-3.

Widnes Town were up next at home with Bilston putting in their most dominant performance of the season to record a 7-0 win. Jordan Crump put Bilston ahead on 14 minutes with Harry Dixon adding another ten minutes later. Ben Priest made it three just before the break with the game over as a contest in a blistering spell at the start of the second half. Nathaniel Hewett scored two minutes into the half before Crump got his second to make it five goals just two minutes later. Dixon made it six just 60 seconds later with Callum Bright adding the seventh just before the hour.

Bilston have lost just once in the league this season, that coming in the first midweek of the season, and they made it six games unbeaten with a 3-0 home win over Market Drayton Town. Harry Dixon put Bilston ahead in the very first minute of the game, but we had to wait until four minutes into the second half for the next goal when Jordan Crump doubled the lead. Darragh Bustin rounded off the scoring with the third midway through the half.

The fourth and final game of the month saw them travel to Stafford Town in the Macron Cup, and they progressed to the next round with a 2-0 win. Nathan Guest opened the scoring on 36 minutes with Harry Dixon adding the second a minute before the break.

Bilston just edged out Wolverhampton Casuals who had two wins and two draws in the month. Barnton, Foley Meir and Sandbach all had an unbeaten month also but draws hindered them.

Total Games played in the Month: 4Total Points won in the Month: 12Average: 3.00

Congratulations to all of the winners.

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 9
articles.meta: Thu 1st October 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
We’re back for another week, and another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. Macron Cup the main focus

This past weekend saw no league games of any kind take place, which is astonishingly rare in the NWCFL. Instead, teams from all three divisions competed against one another in the First Round proper of the league’s premier cup competition, the Macron Cup.

Highlights included Alsager Town, Telford Town, Wednesfield Community and Wolverhampton Casuals all winning after nail-biting penalty shootouts; a battle of the First Division South newcomers Crewe and Brereton Social that finished 6-0 to the former on home soil; and the late kick-off between FC Isle of Man, of the Premier Division, and Widnes Town, from the South, finishing the same way as Crewe/Brereton.

2. Trafford dreaming of Wembley

We’re going back slightly longer than a week to discuss this next point, but Trafford, of the Premier Division, absolutely merit some praise for the result they managed a week ago on Saturday in the Emirates FA Cup. Only they and South Liverpool were left in the competition at the time of this 2nd Qualifying Round – pressure? What pressure?

Going up against Heaton Stannington, of the Northern Premier League, and doing so away from home in Newcastle upon Tyne, no less, Tom Baker’s team strode into the third qualifying round with a 2-1 win thanks to goals by Kyle Worsley and Brad Byrne. Due to South’s exit at the hands of Warrington Town, Trafford are the last NWCFL side in the competition. They will face Atherton Collieries this coming Saturday, knowing just two more wins will see them in the First Round proper.

3. Repeat of last season’s North in the Prem?

To look at the top of the NWCFL Premier Division table right now is to experience déjà vu for anyone who kept themselves up to date with the progress of the promotion race in the First Division North last season. Nelson, who were eventual champions, are currently second, and Droylsden, the runners-up who won the play-offs, are sitting pretty at the top.

Credit where it’s due, the Bloods look like would-be champions right now. They’ve lost just once in the league this season – the only team to hold such a distinction – and have also only dropped points on one other occasion so far in 2026/27. Nelson are a mere point behind, having won seven of their nine league games thus far. These two sides were the ones who broke away from a very crowded title chase in the North last season – might they both do it again?

4. Home is where the points are for the top two in the North

Woe betides any team that must travel to either the DT Hughes Community Stadium, or the OWS Engineering Stadium anytime soon – no pressure, Colne or Garstang. Maghull, currently top of the tree in the First Division North, and Cammell Laird 1907, breathing down their necks in second, have both played six home league games this season, and haver earned maximum points in each and every one of them.

The only other team in the entire NWCFL who can say the same about their home record at this stage is AFC Bridgnorth, in the First Division South. It was a badge of honour for them that they had also made an entirely unbeaten start to life in the First Division South this season, until…

5. AFC Bridgnorth finally beaten

Granted, this entry also comes from a result that happened almost two weeks ago now, but I was on holiday, and it’s absolutely still worth mentioning here. AFC Bridgnorth settled into their debut campaign in the NWCFL at record speed in the South, going unbeaten in their first seven league games. Game number eight came on the 19th of September.

Facing off against fellow new boys Brereton Social at their opponents’ Red Lion Ground, Bridgnorth were finally undone in the NWCFL for the first time in a 1-0 defeat to the side currently sitting 14th in the table. Incredibly, this was Brereton’s first home win of the season – what a time to get it!

articles.title: Maghull - PST Sport First Division North Club of the Month
articles.meta: Tue 29th September 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Maghull have been presented with their PST Sport Club of the Month award for August in the First Division North after once again starting the season in blistering fashion. League Committee Member Sid Blain popped along to Maghull on Saturday ahead of their Macron Cup win over AFC Knowsley and is pictured presenting the award to Manager Joe Burns.

Maghull ended August sitting proudly at the top of the league. After losing their first game of the season, they romped to victory in their next eight games, scoring a whopping 26 goals in the month and conceded just eight.

They started the season with a trip to Darwen with Nathan Moffitt putting them ahead on 7 minutes. However the home side turned it around to win 2-1 with two late goals, the winner coming just two minutes from time.

They bounced back with a 1-0 home win against AFC Blackpool, Jamie Clark's penalty on 69 minutes the difference, before beating Holker Old Boys 4-1 at home. Holker took an early lead with Wil Hoey levelling before the break. Connor Rankin put Maghull ahead just before the hour, with two late goals from Sam Smith giving them the win.

Next came an impressive 3-0 midweek win at Ashton Town, Sam Smith scoring once in each half with a penalty from Jamie Clark in stoppage time being the icing on the cake. A trip to Uppermill was next and they fell behind in the first half. However Ayden Garrigan levelled after an hour with Connor Rankin scoring the winner for Maghull in a 2-1 win in the last minute of the game.

Maghull's next game was at home to Ashton Athletic with Nathan Moffitt putting them ahead midway through the half. However just a minute later Ashton levelled. Sam Smith's fifth goal of the season put them back ahead before half time, with Nathan Peet and Jacob Till securing a 4-1 win in the second half. A third clean sheet of the month came at Garstang next in a 3-0 win. Connor Rankin scored just after half an hour, with another Jamie Clark penalty making it 2-0 six minutes into the second half. Nathan Peet scored the final goal

Perhaps the performance of the month came in the next game at home to Maine Road, a 5-1 victory being their biggest of the month. They went ahead through Connor Rankin on 16 minutes with their opponents levelling shortly after. It stayed that was until just after the hour when a quickfire double from Nathan Moffitt put them in control before Rankin added his second of the game with 20 minutes to go. A Harry Long goal in the last minute outlined their superiority.

The final game came at home to AFC Knowsley on Bank Holiday Monday, with a superb crowd of 455 watching what was a local derby. Knowsley took an early lead before a double from Nathan Peet turned things around, although scores were level at the break when Knowsley equalised just before the break. Maghull secured what was their eighth successive win with Connor Rankin making it 3-2 on the hour.

That gave them 27 points from their 9 games for a 3.00 average.

Cammell Laird 1907 had a good month after their switch to the North with five wins and two draws in their eight games. Woolton had four wins and three draws, with Darwen also having four wins in the month.

Total Games played in the Month: 9Total Points won in the Month: 27Average: 3.00

First Division South - AFC Bridgnorth

The winner of the Club of the Month in the First Division South are AFC Bridgnorth, their first month in the NWCFL being impressive after being laterally moved from the Midland League.

They spoke pre-season that the move to our league could benefit them with more local games than last season, and they have started the season with five wins and two draws from their seven games. They have also done it in style with 20 goals scored, scoring three or more goals in five of their seven games in the month.

Their first NWCFL game came at home to Foley Meir, with Sam Preece scoring in first half stoppage time to open their account. Foley levelled in the opening stages of the second half, but a late double from Suar Dedja - both goals coming in the final six minutes - gave them their first three points.

It was a win that obviously gave them confidence, as a midweek trip to Bilston Town saw them return with a 4-0 win. Kobi Love put them ahead on 20 minutes before another quick Suar Dedja double made it three, this time his goals coming in the last five minutes of the first half. A strong performance was highlighted when Craig Tuckley added a fourth midway through the second half.

The third game was Bilston Town again, this time at home in the Edward Case Cup. It looked like a repeat was on the cards with Mitchell Evans and Craig Tuckley making it 2-0 with less than an hour played, however Bilston hit back this time to secure a 2-2 draw. That meant penalties with AFC Bridgnorth winning 4-1 from the spot. Their first league points were dropped in the next game which was a 1-1 draw at Wednesfield Community. The home side went ahead with just 18 minutes to go, but Bridgnorth showed their grittiness with a leveller four minutes later.

They returned to winning ways with a 4-1 win at home to Crewe, but it was not all plain sailing, especially when Crewe went ahead after two minutes. Michael Williams levelled after 15 minutes, and it remained that way until Suar Dedja put them ahead on 64 minutes. It took a late double from Nehemia Zazi to secure the win, both his goals coming in the last ten minutes.

A trip to Alsager Town was next, with the home side taking the lead before Suar Dedja's penalty on the half hour making it one each. Bridgnorth went in at the break ahead with Sam Preece scoring just before the whistle, and Preece then made it 3-1 at the start of the second half. Another from Alsager just after the hour made it interesting, but they could not find an equalier, Bridgnorth winning 3-2.

The seventh final game of the month saw them host New Mills, another game where they won 3-2 but this time having to twice come from behind. The Millers scored early before Suar Dedja equalised on 17 minutes. Just before half time New Mills went ahead only for Mitchell Evans to level just before the hour. With a draw looking likely, David Anani hit the winner three minutes from time.

That gave them 20 points from their 7 games for a 2.86 average.

Closest to them was Eccleshall with six wins from eight games, with Wolverhampton Casuals winning five of their seven games. Brereton Social also started well with three wins before tailing off as the month progressed.

Total Games played in the Month: 7Total Points won in the Month: 20Average: 2.86

Congratulations to all of the winners.

articles.title: Week 9: Summary
articles.meta: Sat 26th September 2026 | Match Reviews | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
MACRON CUP FIRST ROUND

The Macron Cup took centre stage on Saturday with 60 of our sides in action on Friday night and Saturday afternoon.

Burscough entertained Cammell Laird 1907 on the Friday night, with Callum Laird scoring the only goal of the game for the Premier Division side as they progressed into the next round.

Onto Saturday, and that pattern continued, with not one Premier Division side knocked out by sides from the North or South divisions.

The biggest win of the day was 6-0 which occurred in two of the games. The first came at Crewe who notched their biggest win since joining the league in the summer as they beat Brereton Social with Joshua Maris grabbing a hat-trick. The second was the later kick off over at FC Isle of Man where there was another hat-trick, Adam Adebiyi taking home the matchball after his team beat Widnes Town.

Goals were aplenty on the day with Will Sim also getting a hat-trick for Fulwood Amateurs as they beat Colne 5-0. Benni Smalls-Braithwaite also grabbed three for Flixton as they beat Uppermill 4-0, that their fifth successive win, with Joe Bacon also hitting three for Atherton LR as they won 5-2 away at Abbey Hey.

New Mills also hit five as they beat Maine Road 5-0, Finlay Dooner with a brace. Luke Hepple also scored twice for Nelson as they won 4-1 at Steeton, with Thomas Scarborough doing likewise for FC St Helens as they won by the same scoreline at South Liverpool.

Others to hit four were Charnock Richard, who came from 2-1 down to beat Longridge Town 4-2, whilst there was the same scoreline at Squires Gate where Euxton Villa scored twice in the last two minutes to win . Ramsbottom United and Maghull both won 4-0 against Cheadle Heath Nomads and AFC Knowsley respectively.

Eccleshall left it late to beat Shawbury United 4-2 with two goals in the last two minutes. Maxwell Chimenes scored two penalties for the Eagles. Halewood Apollo beat Ashton Town 3-0, with Holker Old Boys beating Garstang by the same scoreline.

Litherland REMYCA won 3-1 at home to Ashton Athletic, with Allscott Heath winning by the same scoreline at Market Drayton Town. Another 3-1 came at Barnoldswick Town who beat AFC Blackpool, whilst Bacup Borough were 3-0 winners at home to Thornton Cleveleys.

Irlam made it six successive wins as they beat Glossop North End 1-0, Jack Mitchell with the only goal there. Bilston Town are seven games unbeaten and they progressed with a 2-0 win at Stafford Town. There was also a 2-0 at the Butchers Arms as Chadderton beat Droylsden.

Barnton won 2-1 at Daisy Hill, Bailey Sherlock and Thomas Stanton with goals for them in the last five minutes, with Woolton beating Ashville 2-1. Another 2-1 came at Prestwich Heys who beat Trafford.

Four games were decided on penalties, the most thrilling coming at Telford Town where AFC Bridgnorth progressed 6-5 from the spot after a 1-1 draw. Wednesfield Community hosted Dawley Town which was also 1-1 with Wednesfield progressing, whilst at Foley Meir it was the away side Wolverhampton Casuals who progressed after a 1-1 draw.

The final game was at Sandbach United who played out a goalless draw with Alsager Town. Penalties then saw Alsager progress 4-2 from the spot.

Today's photo sees Crewe FC players celebrating after scoring one of their goals in the 6-0 win over Brereton Social (@CreweFC on X).

articles.title: Week 9: Manager Quotes
articles.meta: Mon 28th September 2026 | Manager Reactions | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
We're back! And we're speaking again to multiple victorious managers from this weekend's.fixtures in the MWCFL's premier cup competition, the Macron Cup.

Premier Division side Euxton Villa enjoyed themselves on Saturday with a trip to the seaside to face First Division North outfit Squires Gate. Matty Atherton's side ran out 4-2 winners on the coast, with the gaffer saying afterwards: "We're really pleased to progress in the Macron Cup and to get a much needed win after six weeks without one.

"And we were good value for it too, with four goals scored and arguably the man of the match still being the opposition keeper. It was great to see an energy and intensity to our game that has been lacking for a few weeks. Credit to Squires Gate - they scored an excellent equaliser and took it to the wire, but ultimately I think it was the right result on the day.

"We can now look forward to extending our cup run further. Hopefully we can build some momentum on the back of this and start climbing that league table, starting with an important fixture against Abbey Hey next weekend."

Waiting for Villa in the Second Round of this year's Macron Cup will be First Division North side Fulwood Amateurs, who were drawn at home to divisional rivals Colne in the First Round.

Phil Blackwell's side put on a show, putting five past their visitors without reply, and the man in charge had this to say after full time: "We knew the great run of form Colne had been on, so it was really pleasing to be able to come out on top against a very good side.

"It was a fairly even game with regards to possession, but we took our chances at good times and managed to restrict their clear cut opportunities. It's also really pleasing to keep a clean sheet. In the next round, we've got a great draw against Euxton Villa, which will hopefully capture some local interest when it comes around."

One of this weekend's biggest winners were First Division South new arrivals Crewe, who were drawn at home against another side who are making the NWCFL debuts this season in the South, Brereton Social. Joe Pointon and Adam Vickers orchestrated a 6-0 win on home soil for Crewe on Saturday, after which Joe said: "We’ve been threatening to put a performance like that together for a while, so it was really pleasing to see it come together.

"We were only 1-0 up at half-time, but I thought the intensity we played with had earned us the right to go on and really dominate the second half. We kept moving the ball quickly and with purpose, and created a lot of opportunities.

"After the disappointment of last week, it was a brilliant reaction from the players. The challenge now is for us to learn our lessons from the past two weeks and make sure our standards are where they need to be consistently."
